title:
Strain-Driven Optical, Electronic, and Mechanical Properties of Inorganic Halide Perovskite CsGeBr
                    <sub>3</sub>
abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Of late, inorganic perovskite material, especially the lead-free CsGeBr
                    <jats:sub>3,</jats:sub>
                    has gained considerable interest in the green photovoltaic industry due to its outstanding optoelectronic, thermal, and elastic properties. This work systematically investigated the strain-driven optical, electronic, and mechanical properties of CsGeBr
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    through the first-principles density functional theory. The unstrained planar CsGeBr
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    compound demonstrates a direct bandgap of 0.686 at its R-point. However, incorporating external biaxial tensile (compressive) strain can be tuned the bandgap lowering (increasing) to this perovskite. Moreover, due to the increase of tensile (compressive) strain, a red-shift (blue-shift) behavior of the absorption-coefficient and dielectric function is found in the photon energy spectrum. Strain-induced mechanical properties also reveal that CsGeBr
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    perovskites are mechanically stable and highly malleable material and can be made suitable for photovoltaic applications. The strain-dependent optoelectronic and mechanical behaviors of CsGeBr
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    explored here would benefit its future applications in optoelectronics and photovoltaic cells design.
                  </jats:p>
journal: ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology
